key_insight: PhysDial shows that training on trajectories with changing physical conditions helps pretrained video models predict PDE responses to interventions, rather than merely accept condition inputs.
engineering_relevance: Condition-responsive learned simulators could support control, design, and what-if studies involving changes in forcing or physical parameters.
method: Adapt a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families.
Encode coefficients alongside noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equations as text prompts.
Train with within-trajectory switches and evaluate predictions against changed solver branches from the same state.
evidence_signal: In Kolmogorov flow, within-trajectory switches comprised about 5% of training samples and halved post-change error at matched compute for forcing wavenumber or amplitude changes.
watch_item: Condition responsiveness depends on training coverage; the reported two-dimensional experiments do not establish reliability for unseen interventions or three-dimensional turbulence.
paper_title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
